{"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income / rent payment protection in housing","requirement":"The NJ Law Against Discrimination prohibits housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. A landlord cannot deny a lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.","key_value":"Cannot deny rental based solely on Section 8 voucher / lawful source of income","coverage_conditions":"Applies to the sale or rental of all property including open land, for business or residential purposes.","exemptions":"Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as his/her residence at the time of rental; rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as residence at the time of rental; preference given to persons of the same religion by a religious organization.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":{"any":[{"all":[{"field":"units","op":"==","value":2},{"field":"owner_occupied","op":"==","value":true}]},{"all":[{"field":"units","op":"==","value":1},{"field":"owner_occupied","op":"==","value":true}]}]}},"subject":"landlord","interaction":null,"yields_to_local":false,"preempts_local":false,"effective_date":null,"effective_rule":null,"enacted_date":null,"end_date":null,"penalty":null,"citation":"N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq.","quoted_span":"The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.","supporting_spans":["This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the

income."],"confidence":0.8,"conflict_note":null}],"notes":"The brochure is a NJ Division on Civil Rights summary of the Law Against Discrimination. Only the source-of-income provision falls in scope (screening_restrictions). The rest (protected classes, service animal fees, complaint procedures) is general anti-discrimination or procedure and was ignored. The service-dog fee limit is not an application or upfront-fee cap. The statute citation is the general LAD cite (N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq.), inferred from the document's reference to N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm; the document gives no effective date."}
